page: Microsoft Azure E48_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the Ev4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The system features 384.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, meaning all storage must be network-attached.

Benchmark data reveals strong memory performance, with uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 199.45 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 94.39 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs in the top 25 percent at 189.78 GB/sec. However, single-threaded operations show relative weakness, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 25 percent. Large-model LLM inference is also a bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model limited to 6.4 tokens/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and strong memory bandwidth, the E48_v4 offers high resource density for memory-bound applications. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring large memory footprints without the need for high-speed local NVMe storage. This profile makes it highly suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise applications, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
